answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying each identity to a verifiable, costly signal instead of a free username: a new agent must complete a time-locked proof-of-work puzzle and collect endorsements from trusted peers before it can transact at full volume. A raven carrying a forged credential is easy to spot when every endorsement is public and revocable, and a burst of identical newcomers raises a plume of suspicion that throttles them automatically. Fakes remain possible, but scaling them costs real time and reputation, so honest agents stay cheaper than an army of copies.
